title: Turnkey Exhibition Services UAE | Scope & Handover | FANN
description: Coordinate exhibition stand design, fabrication and site work in the UAE. Define responsibilities, venue services, changes and dismantling before approving the scope.
heading: Turnkey exhibition services in the UAE
intro: FANN coordinates exhibition stand design, production, logistics, venue submissions, installation and removal in the UAE within an agreed project scope. Turnkey means connecting these stages, not assuming that every supplier, venue charge or after-show service is included.

sections.heading: One brief, with a named owner for each hand-off
sections.text: Start with the show, venue, hall, allocated dimensions, open sides and current exhibitor manual. Add product displays, meeting space, storage, brand assets and the people authorised to approve drawings and changes. FANN coordinates from its Dubai office, with fabrication supported by its in-house workshop in Umm Al Quwain.
items: Design release: agree the drawing revision, dimensions, materials, finishes and graphics.
Production release: connect the approved design to the fabrication specification and required review points.
Site handover: confirm access, transport, installation sequence and responsibility for venue submissions.
After-show handover: specify dismantling, return transport and any storage or reuse work.

sections.heading: Separate stand work from venue and exhibitor services
sections.text: An itemised proposal should show what FANN supplies, what another supplier provides and what the exhibitor orders directly. Electricity, internet, rigging, AV, furniture and product delivery need explicit responsibility and inclusion checks. The word turnkey alone does not establish a venue appointment, a utility order or an approval outcome.
items: Mark each scope item included, excluded or supplied by others.
Name the party responsible for ordering and paying for venue services.
Identify equipment dimensions, delivery contacts and installation interfaces before site access.
Use the current show instructions rather than assuming a previous manual applies.

sections.heading: Use the actual show programme to sequence work
sections.text: Show opening is not the deadline for drawings, production or site access. Work backwards through organiser submissions, design decisions, material release, graphics and installation. FANN plans against the actual show and agreed scope; a fixed production duration cannot be confirmed before the drawings, materials and schedule are reviewed.

sections.heading: Keep changes tied to drawings and scope
sections.text: When a product display, graphic, finish or layout changes, identify the affected drawing revision and ask what has already been released. Confirm the effect on materials, submissions, price and schedule before proceeding. An updated visual is not, by itself, agreement to extra work or evidence of approval.

sections.heading: Close the job with an after-show plan
sections.text: Before approving the proposal, state which items will be removed, retained, returned or considered for reuse. Record the destination, collection responsibility and any handling or storage requirements. Dismantling and storage are separate scope decisions, not automatic promises attached to every design-and-build enquiry.

faqs.question: Does turnkey mean every exhibition expense is included?
faqs.answer: No. Turnkey describes coordination across the agreed stages; the itemised proposal defines what is included. Check design, fabrication, graphics, transport, submissions, installation and removal separately. Name any venue services or third-party items supplied by others, and settle exclusions before approving the work rather than treating the label as an all-inclusive package.

faqs.question: Who orders electricity, internet or rigging for the stand?
faqs.answer: The responsible party must be named in the project scope. Send the current exhibitor manual and list the services your stand needs. Confirm who orders each service, who pays the provider and who connects it to the build. Do not assume a stand quotation automatically includes venue charges or specialist supplier work.

faqs.question: Can an overseas exhibitor coordinate a UAE build remotely?
faqs.answer: Yes. FANN can coordinate design, production, logistics, venue submissions, installation and removal locally within the agreed scope. Send your allocation, current manual, product requirements and approval contacts. Agree who can release drawings and changes, and identify any product shipping or exhibitor tasks that remain with your own team or appointed suppliers.

faqs.question: What happens if the brief changes after production is released?
faqs.answer: A change needs a scope and schedule check before work continues. Identify the affected drawing, finish, graphic or product requirement and confirm what is already committed. FANN reviews the change against materials, production and the show schedule; any revised work, cost or delivery arrangement should be agreed rather than assumed.

faqs.question: Are dismantling, storage and reuse included in a turnkey quote?
faqs.answer: Only the after-show services listed in the agreed quotation are included. State what needs dismantling, where retained items should go and whether transport, storage or reuse planning is required. Reuse depends on the components, condition and next allocation; do not assume every stand or graphic can be stored and used again unchanged.
